title: The Biggest Digit-Sum Groups

concept.title: Group by a computed key, then count the groups
body: Group the numbers `1, 2, ..., n` by the **sum of their digits**: 13 and 31 are in the same group (digit sum 4). A hash map with the digit sum as the key counts the members of each group. Afterwards find the **largest group size**, and count how many groups have that size.

The key does not have to be the number itself: any value you can compute from the element (digit sum, remainder, sorted letters) can group things. Here the key is at most `9 * 6 = 54`, so a small array would work as well as a map.

statement: Put the numbers 1, 2, ..., n into groups: two numbers are in the same group if the sums of their digits are equal. Print how many groups have the largest size.
outputFormat: Print the number of groups of the largest size.
hints: Compute the digit sum of every number from 1 to n.
Count how many numbers have each digit sum.
Find the largest count and count how many digit sums reach it.

explanation: A map from digit sum to the number of members gives the group sizes; the groups of the largest size are then counted.
solution.complexity: Time O(n log n), space O(1) (at most 54 groups).

code.python:
n = int(input())

size = {}
for x in range(1, n + 1):
    s = 0
    y = x
    while y > 0:
        s += y % 10
        y //= 10
    size[s] = size.get(s, 0) + 1
largest = max(size.values())
print(sum(1 for v in size.values() if v == largest))
